title: Bundle ZXing (or pin it with SRI) and fix sign-out edge cases before real users sign in
description: From the security review of PR #47. (1) Medium: src/index.html loads @zxing/library 0.21.3 from cdn.jsdelivr.net with no integrity attribute, and the CSP allows script-src https://cdn.jsdelivr.net (whole host). The script runs before the app, and the app origin now holds bearer tokens, so a compromised CDN path could read ?code/?invite tokens, wrap fetch/WebSocket, and mint tokens via /auth/refresh. Fix: bundle @zxing/library from npm through Vite (preferred) and drop jsdelivr from script-src; or add SRI + crossorigin and narrow script-src to the exact package path. (2) Low: sign-out doesn't clear the saved invite in sessionStorage (supplyCheckout.invite). (3) Low: a failed POST /auth/sign-out is swallowed and the page redirects anyway, leaving the refresh cookie valid; only redirect on success, else show an error. (4) Hardening: session.js refresh timer with a missing expiresIn gives NaN; default to 3600. (5) Hardening: db.js colls[ev.collection] should use Object.hasOwn.
acceptance_criteria: No third-party script without SRI; CSP script-src has no whole-CDN host; tests for sign-out clearing the invite and for a failed sign-out not redirecting; the artifact build still works in claude.ai.

title: Add atomic, idempotent checkout, return and stock-adjust commands with an inventory movement log
description: Today a checkout saves the sheet line and then bumps stock in a separate read-then-write (src/main.js bumpStock), so a retry or double tap can decrement stock twice, concurrent checkouts on one line can lose a count, and there is no inventory history for the planned stock-drift alarm (docs/journeys.md J4). Add server commands next to the generic document routes (which the edit screens keep using): checkout, return and stock adjust. Each is one DynamoDB transaction that updates the sheet line (server-side ADD on out/returned), stock, a movement record and an operation-ID record; a retry with the same operation ID returns the first result. Server validates integer quantities, returned <= out, prices >= 0 and closed-sheet rules. IAM: add UpdateItem and ConditionCheckItem under the existing LeadingKeys condition. Per-item stock history view. The claude.ai artifact build keeps its two-write path (ADR 0004); this extends ADR 0006 with commands.
acceptance_criteria: Retrying the same operation changes nothing (test); a failure mid-operation leaves nothing half-saved (test); concurrent checkouts on one line never lose a count (test); the nightly drift check can reconcile stock against movements.

title: ADR 0017: company equipment and the ad hoc checkout
description: Owner decisions 2026-09-30. (1) Company equipment: an item is a Supply (used up, charged; today's behavior) or Company equipment (reused, never charged: ladders, cutting mats). Equipment has no client price and keeps a value (what it cost). Inventory gets a Supplies/Equipment filter and, for equipment, a toggle view of what's in and what's out (who, when, which sheet). On a sheet equipment is a separate 'Equipment (not charged)' section with taken and returned, left out of the sheet total and the client CSV. Unreturned equipment is missing, not used: Finished Return stops on equipment still out and asks for each: it's back (return it), still at the job (keep the sheet open), or lost or broken (take it out of storage with that reason in the stock history, and optionally charge the client on that sheet for it, an amount the person enters, which then does appear on the sheet and CSV). (2) Ad hoc checkout: a Quick take on the main screen puts items on the team's one ad hoc sheet (kind 'adhoc', created on the first take, shown apart from job sheets); finishing it counts unreturned supplies as used with no client charge, and the next take starts a new one. Returns from anywhere find where an item is out across open sheets (pick when more than one); a job sheet's 'not on this sheet' dead end offers the sheet where it is out. A line on the ad hoc sheet can move to a job sheet with its counts, in one server transaction, so the client is charged for what was used and stock isn't counted twice. The ADR amends ADR 0014 (every line has a client price; unreturned means used), covers the data model (product kind and value, sheet kind, line kind, damage charge, movement reasons such as lost), the commands and server rules (including the move and the artifact build's path), migration (existing items are supplies, nothing rewritten), and journeys to add to docs/journeys.md.

title: [bug] npm run land hangs forever when the PR's CI fails

title: Record journey videos from the tagged tests instead of a separate script

title: Post-deploy smoke checks and on-demand canary in the deploy workflow
description: After each deploy, run the read-only checks the lead has been running by hand: /me and /ops/teams return 401 without a token, the auth. domain serves Managed Login, the realtime endpoint resolves, no alarm is in ALARM, and the core journey canary (pkt) runs once on demand whatever the hour (ADR 0012). title: Deploy workflow: publish the web app and demo from the release build, and check the edge router

After any web deploy or publish, run aws cloudfront test-function against the LIVE router for app., the apex, /demo/ and www (the check from the qk1.1 outage), fetch config.json and check its keys and the CSP header; roll the app channel back to the previous release on failure. title: Deploy workflow: stateful stacks behind a second approval and a no-replacement check

Deploy them in the same workflow only when their diff is non-empty, after a separate environment approval, and fail before deploying if the change set replaces or deletes a table, user pool, key, bucket, hosted zone or log group (parse the CloudFormation change set; allow an explicit override input for planned migrations). It assumes the OIDC deploy role, synths once, posts each stack's cdk diff to the job summary, and deploys the stateless stacks in dependency order: web, then api and realtime, then observability and email, in us-east-1 (region from config, us-west-2 is phase 2). Honour backupCopy=false while there's no backup account (ADR 0003). Needs a security review (IAM, OIDC, workflow permissions: id-token write only in this job, no pull_request_target, pinned action SHAs).

title: Operator group changes (AdminAddUserToGroup, AdminRemoveUserFromGroup) never reach EventBridge, so they don't alert
description: 2026-09-27 drill after the trail (3sv.3; trail logging since 21:29 ET): the owner added operator alert-test at 21:30:35 ET (AdminCreateUser), 21:30:36 (AdminAddUserToGroup), then removed it at 21:33:40 (AdminRemoveUserFromGroup) and deleted it. CloudTrail lookup-events has all four. aws events test-event-pattern with the real CloudTrail events wrapped as EventBridge events: all three match the live supply-checkout-prod-operator-pool-changes pattern. But MatchedEvents/TriggeredRules/Invocations for the rule = 1 (21:30, AdminCreateUser only; the owner got that P1 email and no others) after 20+ minutes. So the group events never arrived on the default bus. Next: owner creates a temporary diagnostic rule (source aws.cognito-idp, all detail-types) targeting a CloudWatch Logs group, repeats add/remove with a throwaway operator, and we compare what arrives (detail-type, source, eventName, any read-only/insight flags); check whether these calls are logged as management write events in the trail's S3 files; check AWS docs/known issues on Cognito events delivered to EventBridge; consider rule state ENABLED_WITH_ALL_CLOUDTRAIL_MANAGEMENT_EVENTS if they are classed read-only; last resort an alternative signal (a periodic list-users-in-group diff Lambda alerting on membership change).
acceptance_criteria: Adding and removing a test operator's group membership each delivers a P1 email; root cause written in docs/infrastructure.md Operators.
notes: CloudTrail classification is identical for AdminCreateUser (delivered) and AdminAddUserToGroup/AdminRemoveUserFromGroup/AdminDeleteUser (not delivered): eventType AwsApiCall, readOnly false, managementEvent true, eventCategory Management, same endpoint. So read-only classification (ENABLED_WITH_ALL_CLOUDTRAIL_MANAGEMENT_EVENTS) is not the explanation. The diagnostic catch-all rule is the next step.

title: Create a CloudTrail trail: every 'AWS API Call via CloudTrail' alert is silent without one
description: Found 2026-09-27 during the operator check: creating operator dave-test (AdminCreateUser, AdminAddUserToGroup) matched the supply-checkout-prod-operator-pool-changes pattern exactly (source, eventSource, pool ID, no invokedBy) but TriggeredRules stayed empty and no P1 arrived. The prod account has no CloudTrail trail (describe-trails --include-shadow-trails is empty), and EventBridge docs: 'To record events with one of the CloudTrail detail-type values, you must enable a CloudTrail trail with logging.' So every CloudTrail-based rule is dead: operator pool/self-service, audit watch, alert route, alarm changes, rule tampering, deletions and backup change rules. Add a trail in CDK (all regions, management events read+write, log file validation, S3 bucket with SSE-KMS, block public access, TLS-only policy, lifecycle/retention per the infosec policy, access logging to the logs bucket), in the stack that fits (observability or a new audit stack), with cdk-nag clean, and make sure the alert-route rule's StopLogging/DeleteTrail/UpdateTrail watch names it. Consider an organization trail from the management account later (owner decision). After deploy, rerun the operator drill: add/remove a test operator and confirm the P1 arrives.
acceptance_criteria: Trail in CDK with tests; after the owner's deploy, get-trail-status IsLogging true, and an operator add sends a P1 email; security review approves.
notes: 2026-09-27 verified after the owner's deploy (data, audit, observability): trail supply-checkout-prod-trail logging, multi-region, global events, log file validation; first delivery 21:32 ET, digest delivered, no errors. Owner added operator alert-test at 21:30 ET: supply-checkout-prod-operator-pool-changes TriggeredRules 1, Invocations 1, FailedInvocations 0.

title: operators CLI: aws can't read --cli-input-json file:///dev/stdin on macOS

title: Operator admin CLI and skill: add, list, disable, remove and reset operators in one command

title: Alarm when the web app is down: CloudFront 5xx rate and router function errors
description: On 2026-09-27 app. and /demo/ returned 503 for ~90 minutes (qk1.1: router SyntaxError after the web deploy) and no alarm fired: nothing watches the distribution or its CloudFront Function. Add a P1 alarm on the distribution's 5xxErrorRate (with a minimum request count so a quiet night doesn't page) and on the router function's FunctionExecutionErrors/FunctionThrottles (AWS/CloudFront, Region=Global, us-east-1), routed like the journey alarms, with a runbook entry (rollback: redeploy the previous web stack commit). Consider also a deploy check that runs aws cloudfront test-function on the router after a web deploy.

title: Run CodeQL on beads-only PRs (the code_scanning rule needs it) and name that rule when land is blocked
description: Found landing #157 (first beads-only PR after #154): CI passed green but mergeStateStatus stayed BLOCKED because main's ruleset has a code_scanning rule (CodeQL, errors / medium+) and #154 made the codeql job skip when beads_only, so the PR has no CodeQL analysis. npm run land misdiagnosed it as require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes (#153, same authors, merged fine). title: Skip the heavy CI jobs when a change only touches the beads export
description: pbp.13 makes the lead land a beads-export PR after most merges and bead edits, and each one currently runs the full CI (4 browser jobs on the PR, all 12 plus infra and backend on the push to main, plus CodeQL). In ci.yml's changes job, output beads_only=true when every changed file is .beads/issues.jsonl, for pull_request, merge_group and push (push compares with HEAD^1; nightly, manual and workflow_call runs always run everything). Jobs that can't be affected by the export (test matrix, codeql, infra, backend, regions, dependencies, workflows, lint and scripts if they don't read .beads) skip when beads_only. Keep pr-title, the secrets/gitleaks scan and the public-safety check running, since bead text is public. CI passed still reports and succeeds when the jobs are skipped.
acceptance_criteria: A beads-only PR finishes CI with only the cheap jobs and a green CI passed; any other change (including ci.yml itself) runs the same jobs as today; the push to main after a beads-only merge skips the browser matrix; docs/testing.md or README CI section explains the rule; actionlint passes.

title: Keep the beads export and the backlog page current automatically
description: Owner request (2026-09-27): the backlog must always be current in both formats, .beads/issues.jsonl for machines and the private backlog page for humans, with no manual step. pbp.12 only added reminders. (1) npm run land: after merging a PR that isn't itself the export PR, rebuild the backlog page and, if the export is stale, run the beads:pr flow automatically after the land lock is released (no nested-lock deadlock); opt out with an env var. (2) Bead edits outside a merge (bd create/update/close) also make both stale, and the page can only be republished with Claude's Artifact tool. Add a committed Claude Code Stop hook (.claude/settings.json + a script) that, only in the main checkout, rebuilds the page when bead data changed since the last publish and blocks the stop with a reason telling the lead to republish it (and to run npm run beads:pr when the export is stale). npm run backlog:published records the published page's data hash (excluding the generated timestamp) in a gitignored stamp so the hook stops asking; respect stop_hook_active to avoid loops. No artifact URL or emails in the repo.
acceptance_criteria: land rebuilds the page and lands the export PR itself when stale (test in land-pr.test.sh / beads-pr.test.sh); the Stop hook blocks only when the page's data differs from the published stamp or the export is stale, only in the main checkout, never twice in a row (node tests); CLAUDE.md and docs updated; test:scripts and public-safety pass.

title: Fix the flaky 'two lands at once' test in land-pr.test.sh
description: After #144 merged, CI's Shell scripts job failed on PR #138 (run 36331091651): in 'two lands at once run one after the other', the second land printed 'Waiting for the land of #42' then 'PR #43 was not merged.' with no other output and exit 0 recorded as failed checks (the second land exits 0 / takes the lock after / merges). description: The repo is owned by a personal account, so GitHub's merge queue isn't available. Two lead sessions landing at once keep pushing each other's PRs behind main (#131 gave up after 3 updates). Add a cross-worktree lock to scripts/land-pr.sh, like tests/run-lock.js (stale-lock detection by PID, a clear 'waiting for land of #N' message), so only one land runs at a time, and raise the behind-main retry limit. Keep the merge-queue path for when the repo moves to an organization.

title: Run the artifact import for the family business
description: Owner task after PR #129 and the prod deploy: export the artifact's 'Everything (JSON)', run import-artifact against prod for their team, dry run first then --apply.

title: Cancel the Stripe subscription when a team closes

PR #103 review: also delete or anonymise the Stripe customer record, and make sure a webhook for a purged team can never recreate its META item.

Check this bead against the stripe_implementation_planner plan described there.

title: Record a linked user's email only after a verified code, not at refresh
description: PR #104 review F1: any state kept in Cognito can be throttled via the shared user-update quota, so windows A/B can be forced. Replace the trigger's refresh-time recording with a positive signal: POST /me/email/verify (PR #105) writes custom:linked_email only when VerifyUserAttribute succeeds; the trigger never records at refresh. Also F2: document that the HMAC log key is visible via lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration and drift detection.
acceptance_criteria: The trigger no longer writes custom:linked_email at refresh/API sign-in; the verify route records it after a successful code; tests show a rewritten address can never become recorded without a code; security review.
notes:
PR #105 review: preferred design (a) — after VerifyUserAttribute succeeds, the account function re-reads GetUser and, if email_verified is true, writes a VERIFIED_EMAIL item (lowercased address + time) in the caller's USER# partition with its existing scoped role; the trigger records custom:linked_email at refresh only when the current email equals that item (adds a scoped DynamoDB read to the trigger role). Avoid granting the account function AdminUpdateUserAttributes. Check live in 3hh whether a code stays valid after email changes. Also: with keepOriginal, a native email change keeps email_verified true for the old address, so /me shows verified while a new address awaits its code — consider a pending-address signal.
PR #105: for a user with downgrade_pending, a correct code doesn't clear the flag; only a Managed Login sign-in clears it (and unverifies again). With the positive VERIFIED_EMAIL signal, a code-verified address should also clear the flag at the next refresh.

title: Harden the linked-email downgrade against a failed write
description: PR #97 review F1: if the Managed Login downgrade of email_verified fails (possibly forced by flooding UpdateUserAttributes to hit the shared quota), a refresh from another session records the rewritten address as verified, reopening /me invite listing and reverse capture. Retry the downgrade once within the 5 s budget; add an admin-only custom:downgrade_pending flag written first so the refresh path refuses to record while set, cleared on successful downgrade; add a hashed-sub correlation handle to the failure log and an EmailUnverifyFailures runbook step (clear custom:linked_email, set email_verified=false); document the throttling vector.
acceptance_criteria: Tests show a failed downgrade followed by a refresh never records the rewritten address; runbook step documented; security review.

title: Make artifact checkout and return retries count once
description: In the artifact build, Try again after a lost answer or the new 20 s timeout recomputes from the latest sheet and calls bumpStock again, so a checkout or return can count twice (PR #95).
acceptance_criteria: A checkout or return retried after a lost answer or timeout counts once in the artifact build (e.g. a per-action mark like savedReceipts); tests in both builds.

title: Make receipt saves to existing sheets idempotent
description: Saving a receipt to an existing sheet writes absolute out values computed from the latest copy of the sheet, so a retry after a lost answer or false conflict can count receipt lines twice; new sheets from a receipt get a fresh ID each attempt (PR #90).
acceptance_criteria: A receipt saved again after a lost answer or timeout adds each line to an existing sheet once and creates each new sheet once (an operation-ID 'add lines' command in the web build); tests in both builds; security review if backend changes.

title: Keep cost on sheet lines written by sheet updates
description: backend/src/data/sheets.ts line() keeps only code, name, price, out and returned, so in the web build the cost a receipt writes onto sheet lines via the ordinary sheet update is silently dropped (PR #83). The checkout command keeps it.
acceptance_criteria: The SheetLine validator accepts optional cost using the shared money rule (0–1,000,000, at most two decimals) and stores it; tests for keeping it and rejecting a bad value; fake-aws mirrors it; security review done.

title: Protect backup copies with an SCP on the backup account
description: PR #80 review: a backup-account admin can destroy copies without deleting recovery points by scheduling deletion of / disabling / rewriting the vault KMS key, or replacing the vault access policy. Add an SCP from the management account on the backup account denying kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion, kms:DisableKey, kms:PutKeyPolicy on the backup keys and backup:PutBackupVaultAccessPolicy, DeleteBackupVaultAccessPolicy, DeleteBackupVaultLockConfiguration, DeleteBackupVault on supply-checkout-* vaults, except a break-glass role. Alternatively evaluate a logically air-gapped vault. Owner deploys (management account).
acceptance_criteria: SCP defined as code (or documented JSON) and attached to the backup account; a test or dry run shows the denied actions fail for a normal admin; docs/backups.md records the choice.
notes:
PR #121 review: the SCP should also protect the backup account's alerting resources — EventBridge rules (DeleteRule/DisableRule/RemoveTargets/PutRule), the copies-missing alarm (DeleteAlarms/DisableAlarmActions), the alert topic and subscriptions, the alert KMS key, and CloudTrail (StopLogging/DeleteTrail).
2026-09-27 from PR #137: also deny on the deletion-records copy bucket in the backup account (except break-glass): s3:PutBucketPolicy, s3:DeleteBucketPolicy, s3:PutBucketOwnershipControls (covers delete), s3:PutBucketObjectLockConfiguration, s3:PutBucketVersioning, likely s3:PutLifecycleConfiguration; and protect rule supply-checkout-<env>-backup-vault-deletions-copy-changes with the other alert rules (DeleteRule, DisableRule, RemoveTargets, PutRule).
close_reason: Superseded: ADR 0003 accepted with the MVP in the prod account only, no backup account. The backup-account stack stays in the code, off (backupCopy=false); reopen when separate accounts return after launch.

title: Set up the backup account and turn on cross-account copies
description: Owner task after PR #80: pick log-archive or a dedicated backup account (ADR 0003 question), then follow docs/backups.md setup.
acceptance_criteria: Org cross-account backup and DynamoDB advanced features are on; the backup-account vault stack is deployed; the SSM parameter /supply-checkout/<env>/backup/copy-vault-arn is set; the first copy job completed within the 3-day lock grace period; verify the backup job metrics carry ResourceType=DynamoDB for the alarms.
notes:
After PR #80: set both SSM parameters /supply-checkout/<env>/backup/copy-vault-arn and /supply-checkout/<env>/backup/organization-id; deploy the backup-account stack with SourceAccountIds, RestoreAccountIds and OrganizationId; the copy vault's compliance lock (30–365 days) becomes permanent 72 h after deploy, so confirm the first copy and KMS access in CloudTrail within that window. title: Keep newer retry marks when the artifact item form saves
description: Follow-up from PR #322 (xb16). In the artifact build the item form writes the whole product from the copy it opened with, so retry marks (ops) that a checkout, return or receipt added to the item while the form was open are dropped; a later retry of that action whose answer was lost could then apply twice to stock. Fix: take ops from the item read at save time (as setCount in src/moves.js now does for stock), with a test in the claude.ai runtime mock where an action's mark lands while the form is open and its retry after the save adds nothing.
acceptance_criteria: A retried checkout/return/receipt whose mark landed while the item form was open is still applied once after the form saves (test, artifact build).

title: Don't let a stale item form undo someone else's stock change

The web build's item form sends a count based on the field it opened with: if the form opened at 10, a checkout takes stock to 8, and someone saves only a price change, the save sends count 10 and undoes the checkout's change (recorded as a count movement, so the history is exact but the number is wrong). Same in the artifact build's whole-document set. Fix: only send a stock change when the person changed the count field; optionally add expectedStock to the stock command so the server refuses with 409 if it moved, and show 'the count changed while you were editing'.
acceptance_criteria: Saving an edit without touching the count never changes stock (test with a live update arriving while the form is open, both builds); a changed count over a moved stock is refused or confirmed.

title: Protect the operator pool itself: deletion protection and alerts on DeleteUserPool, CreateUserPoolDomain

(3) Alert on CreateUserPoolDomain on the ops pool (a second, custom domain doesn't alert today). Keep patterns under the 2,048-character size gate and the tampering watch covering the rule; add drill rows (non-production only).
acceptance_criteria: Deletion protection asserted by a test; pattern tests cover each event; size test passes; docs drill rows; security review.
notes: PR #296 security review: also alert on DeleteManagedLoginBranding and UpdateManagedLoginBranding on the ops pool (the ops client's only style is OpsBranding with the newer managed login; deleting it likely breaks operator sign-in; confirm in the non-production drill). Both carry userPoolId; extend the naming regex in infra/test/observability.test.ts.

In productModal (src/main.js): put 'Comes in packs of' before the count, mark it optional (e.g. placeholder 'Leave blank if bought one at a time'), and give it a hint that receipts add packs x this many to storage; label the count as single items, not packs; when pack size > 1, show a live conversion under the count ('= 2 full packs + 2 loose'). No data or backend change. Both builds.

Backfill once over the app pool (verified emails only), or record it in the email_verified token trigger.

title: Notify the old email address when an account's email changes

Likely built with the CloudTrail detection follow-up, since the change can bypass the API.

title: Send account security notices for changes made directly against Cognito

Detect these wherever they happen: an EventBridge rule on CloudTrail events for the app pool, then a function that looks up the user (AdminGetUser) and sends the notice, like OPERATOR_SELF_SERVICE_EVENTS in the observability stack. First confirm app-pool CloudTrail events identify the user. Alternative: drop email from the web client's writeAttributes and put these operations behind the API.
acceptance_criteria: A password set, TOTP turned on or email changed by a direct Cognito call sends the same notice as the API route (test with recorded CloudTrail event shapes); docs updated; security review.

Fix: at the top of signOut, clearTimeout(timer) and await any in-flight refresh before POST /auth/sign-out. Info: also clear localStorage supplyCheckout.team on sign-out; tighten CSP worker-src to 'self' or 'none' (no workers are used).
acceptance_criteria: Test: sign-out during an in-flight refresh leaves the user signed out on reload; team key cleared; CSP worker-src tightened with its test updated.

Check products[k] lookups and items[k].code (~401) too. Fix with Object.hasOwn, Object.create(null) or Map. keyOf('__proto__') gives '__proto__', which the backend now refuses with 400; show a clear message or map it to a safe key.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: a receipt with barcodes that key to constructor, toString and __proto__ saves correctly or with a clear message, in both builds; no built-in object is modified.

title: Handle built-in object names as product keys in the checkout commands, and oversized sheets

With __proto__ the SDK marshall drops the line but the transaction commits (version bump, movement, stock decrement), so stock moves with no line; constructor/toString resolve to functions, so such products can't be added to a sheet that has items. Fix: Object.hasOwn lookups at commands.ts ~357 and ~461, reject __proto__ in productKey() like checkValue does, build :items without prototype assignment; tests for __proto__ and constructor. (2) Info: commands skip the 350 KB document size check; past 400 KB DynamoDB cancels with ValidationError, which becomes a 500. Map that cancellation on the sheet item to 413 quota_exceeded (TooLargeError) and optionally estimate the new line's size first.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: __proto__ is refused as a product key; a product keyed constructor or toString can be checked out onto a sheet that already has items; an oversized sheet gives 413, not 500.

acceptance_criteria: A Google or Apple user whose provider email is verified can see and accept invites; one whose provider email isn't verified can't (tests); the web client still can't write email_verified.

title: Cut off live updates for removed members and canceled teams within about a minute
description: AppSync Events can't end or filter an open subscription server-side, so a removed member's open connection keeps receiving change notices (collection, ID, op, version; product IDs can be barcodes or names) until it closes: up to 24 h, or under an hour if the client reconnects on token refresh as the contract says. Options from docs/api/realtime.md: per-member channels /users/<sub> with the consumer caching membership for about 60 s (one publish per member per change; departs from ADR 0006), or a rotating team channel /teams/<id>/<epoch> that member removal and billing rotate. Decide and build one. Document contents are already protected by the API's membership check.
acceptance_criteria: A removed member or a canceled team's members receive no further change notices within about 60 s of the change (test).

title: Set one-year log retention on the API functions' log groups
description: The api stack's function log groups get RetentionInDays 731: new LogGroup() sets two years explicitly, so the ObservabilityDefaults aspect (one year) skips them. The realtime stack already sets it explicitly (PR #41). Apply the same one-line fix in the api stack and add an assertion test that every log group in every stack has the intended retention.
acceptance_criteria: Every log group in every stack has one-year retention (assertion test).

title: Deploy a preview stack for each pull request
description: Moved out of qq7 (full CI/CD) to keep the MVP pipeline to staging on merge and prod on release. Per-PR preview stacks per ADR 0012.
acceptance_criteria: Each PR gets a preview URL that's torn down when it closes.

title: Spike: guarantee one region owns a team's writes during home-region takeover
description: Phase-2 takeover (9mn) says the other region updates homeRegion, but on a last-writer-wins global table both regions could accept writes for the same team. Design fencing, for example a lease or epoch, a single-writer authority, or multi-region strong consistency, and record it in ADR 0010.
acceptance_criteria: ADR 0010 records the chosen fencing mechanism and a test plan showing both regions can't accept writes for one team at once.

title: Link Apple and Google sign-ins to an existing account with the same email
description: Without a pre sign-up trigger, signing in with Apple or Google creates a separate Cognito user even when an email/passkey user with the same verified email exists. Add a pre sign-up Lambda that links the federated identity to the existing user (AdminLinkProviderForUser), only when the provider's email is verified.
acceptance_criteria: Signing in with Google or Apple using an email that already has an account lands in that same account and team; an unverified provider email is never linked; tests cover both.

title: Make npm run land explain a blocked PR and fail when it can't merge
description: scripts/land-pr.sh exits 0 after 'PR can't be merged yet: merge state is UNKNOWN', and says nothing when a PR is BLOCKED with every check green because the ruleset needs a human approval (require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes, e.g. release-please PRs authored by github-actions[bot]). It also gave up on UNKNOWN right after another PR merged, when GitHub just hadn't recomputed mergeability yet.
acceptance_criteria: land exits non-zero whenever it doesn't merge. A PR that's BLOCKED with green checks and no approval gets a message naming the approval rule and the gh pr review command. UNKNOWN is retried for a while before giving up. An already-merged PR is reported as merged and cleanup still runs.

title: Confirm App Store and Google Play rules for linking to web checkout
description: ADR 0013 relies on the apps linking owners to Stripe Checkout. Check the current App Store rules for the US storefront (post-2025 ruling) and Google Play's current US rules for external links and any fees, plus what's allowed elsewhere. Record the answer in ADR 0013.
acceptance_criteria:
- Written summary of what each store allows, by country, with links to the current guidelines
- ADR 0013 updated; fallback countries listed
notes: 2026-09-26: research merged in PR #15 (docs/research/app-store-web-checkout.md). Remaining: owner decides Android US (pay Google's 10% external-link fee or show no link), then update ADR 0013 incl. fallback wording.

title: Test store purchases automatically and on real devices
description: StoreKit configuration file tests in CI (iOS simulator), Google Play license testers, sandbox renewals, billing retry, refunds and upgrades between bundles. Run before each mobile release.
acceptance_criteria:
- The 'subscribe in the app' journey has automated coverage on both platforms
- Real-device sandbox purchase checked before each store release

title: Choose a plan in the app and pay on Stripe Checkout
description: Per ADR 0013. Owners-only Plans screen in the iOS and Android apps: plans, seat count, Continue to checkout opens Stripe Checkout in Safari View Controller / Chrome Custom Tab with Apple Pay and Google Pay, app link returns to the app, live update when the webhook lands. Manage plan opens the Customer Portal the same way. Behind a feature flag per platform and country; where the link isn't allowed, show 'Manage your plan on our website' with no prices.

- Non-owners see 'Ask your team owner to upgrade'

title: Add the in-app plan picker and purchase flow with RevenueCat
description: Owners only: Plans screen in the iOS and Android apps with seat bundles, monthly or annual, price, period, trial terms, and links to terms and privacy (App Store 3.1.2). Purchase through @revenuecat/purchases-capacitor, Restore Purchases, and a link to manage the subscription in iOS Settings or the Play Store. Non-owners see 'Ask your team owner to upgrade'. Teams billed elsewhere see where to manage their plan.
acceptance_criteria:
- Sandbox purchase on iOS and Android activates the team within a minute
- Restore Purchases works on a reinstalled app
- Purchase screen passes App Review checklist for subscriptions

title: Enforce one billing source per team and the store-to-web switch
description: A team can have only one active billing source. Web Checkout is blocked while a store subscription is active and vice versa. Switching from store to web: guide the owner to cancel in the store; web billing starts at the end of the store period. Handles Apple's one-subscription-per-group limit (an owner of two teams can buy only one with the same Apple ID).
acceptance_criteria:
- No path in web or app creates a second active subscription for a team (tests)
- Switching from store to web tested end to end with sandbox and Stripe test clocks
close_reason: Superseded: ADR 0013 now uses web billing only (no App Store / Google Play in-app purchase)

title: Process RevenueCat webhooks into team entitlements
description: Per ADR 0013. Webhook endpoint in both regions: check the authorization header, store the event ID for idempotency (WEBHOOK#revenuecat#id), queue on SQS, worker sets billingSource (app_store or play), plan, seatLimit, status and periodEnd. Handles purchase, renewal, cancellation, billing issue, expiration, refund and product change.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each event type tested with RevenueCat sandbox events
- Replayed events change nothing
- Store refunds make the team read-only under the same rules as Stripe

title: Create App Store and Google Play subscription products (seat bundles)
description: Per ADR 0013. One subscription group 'Team plan' with seat-bundle levels (for example Crew 3, Crew 10, Crew 25), monthly and annual, in App Store Connect and Play Console. Family Sharing off. Configure the same products and offerings in RevenueCat, with the team ID as app user ID. Needs Apple and Google organization developer accounts (business entity, D-U-N-S).
acceptance_criteria:
- Products approved and available in both stores' sandbox
- RevenueCat offerings return the bundles in a test build
- Store prices recorded in the tier table
close_reason: Superseded: ADR 0013 now uses web billing only (no App Store / Google Play in-app purchase)

title: Spike: keep sign-in working when us-east-1 is down
description: Cognito doesn't replicate. Compare: accept the limit (tokens keep working), a standby pool with user export and passkey limits, or a multi-region IdP. Recommend one.
acceptance_criteria: - Written recommendation with cost and user impact; ADR if it changes 0007

title: Add feature flags with AWS AppConfig
description: Server-controlled flags so risky features (especially in mobile builds) can be turned off without a release.
acceptance_criteria: - Flag read by the app with caching; flip takes effect within 1 minute

title: Support scheduled payments: annual plans, plan changes and pay by invoice
description: Subscription schedules for plan changes that start at renewal and for annual plans; send-invoice collection (net 30) for customers who pay by invoice.

description: Per ADR 0011. Same web bundle, app icons, splash screens, deep links for invites.

title: Keep an audit log of changes per team
description: Who changed stock, prices, sheets, roles and billing, and when. Owners can view it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every write route records an audit item
- Viewable and filterable by owners
notes: From PR #78: backend/src/data/audit.ts exists but role changes and removals don't write to it; each should write an AUDIT# item (actor, target, from/to role, no emails) in the same transaction.

title: Build and upload the mobile apps from GitHub Actions with fastlane
description: fastlane match for signing, TestFlight and Play internal uploads on each release tag.
acceptance_criteria: - A release tag produces TestFlight and Play internal builds without manual steps

title: Load test the API and live updates
description: Simulate 200 teams at a busy morning peak.

title: Support one-time payments
description: Checkout in payment mode for one-off purchases (for example a receipt pack or setup help), and invoice items added to the next invoice.
acceptance_criteria: - One-time purchase recorded against the team and shown on invoices

title: Find how a team could record another customer's Stripe subscription
description: Follow-up from PR #327 (8jc.17). The purge now sets aside a closed team whose recorded subscription belongs to another Stripe customer (CustomerMismatch) and alarms. Trace every billing worker path that sets stripeSubscriptionId (webhooks, Checkout completion, seat sync, reconcile) and refuse to record a subscription whose customer isn't the team's, with a test; if no path can, document why in docs/infrastructure.md so the set-aside runbook can point to it.
acceptance_criteria: Every path that records a subscription checks its customer (test), or the docs show none can mismatch.

title: Alarm on the pre token generation trigger's errors and throttles
description: Follow-up from PR #312 (8jc.31). The post confirmation trigger now has its own 'Sign-up trigger failing' alarm, but the pre token generation trigger (only when Google or Apple sign-in is on) has a generated function name and no alarm of its own; only the region-wide Functions failing/throttled alarms cover it. Give it a fixed or published name (renaming replaces a live trigger: plan for the brief swap of pool config and invoke permission, e.g. do it before federated sign-in is turned on in prod) and add an Errors+Throttles alarm on the sign-in journey.
acceptance_criteria: Alarm exists with a test; journeys registry and docs list it; the rename plan is documented.

title: Match ops branding calls by branding ID, not only user pool ID
description: From the PR #311 security review. UpdateManagedLoginBranding takes UserPoolId as optional, so a call naming only ManagedLoginBrandingId would log no requestParameters.userPoolId and OperatorPoolChanges would miss it; a large assets upload could also exceed EventBridge's 256 KB event size. Publish the ops branding's ID (CfnManagedLoginBranding.attrManagedLoginBrandingId) via SSM like the pool ID and also match the branding calls on requestParameters.managedLoginBrandingId; or confirm in a non-production drill on a throwaway pool that Cognito refuses the call without --user-pool-id and document it. Impact limited: deletion requires userPoolId and is covered.
acceptance_criteria: Branding calls on the ops branding alert whichever IDs they carry (test), or the drill result documented; size gate passes.

title: Measure the release evidence job's time and size, and add phone-viewport videos if it fits
description: Follow-up from PR #298 (s3c.4). On the first real release, record how long the evidence job took and the size of the uploaded assets (report, videos, traces zip). If too slow or large, lower --pace or keep traces only for failures. If there's room, also record --viewport phone on release so the pack shows the phone layout.
acceptance_criteria: First release's evidence job time and asset sizes recorded here; tuned or phone videos added as the numbers allow.

title: Decide: how a sheet moves from one team to another
description: Owner request 2026-09-30: decide how a sheet (and its lines) can go from one team to another, for example a job handed to a partner company or a crew that works under two teams. Options to weigh: (1) export the sheet as CSV, send it, import it on the other team (no new trust between teams; needs a sheet CSV import, which doesn't exist today, only inventory import); (2) a transfer request that the receiving team's owner approves (and maybe the sending team's owner too), copying or moving the sheet server-side; (3) a share link that lets the other team copy it. For each: cross-team isolation and who can see what (ADR 0005, every read scoped to the caller's team), what happens to stock (the sending team's storage counts, the receiving team's items matched by barcode or created), prices and costs (ADR 0014; costs are internal and must not leak to the other team), company equipment (ADR 0017), whether the original stays (copy) or closes (move), audit trail, billing seats, and the artifact build. Decision only: write an ADR as Proposed; no implementation.

title: Show that a sign-up code was resent
description: On the Managed Login 'Confirm your account' page (auth.), clicking Resend code gives no visual sign that a code was sent. Managed Login is hosted by Cognito: managedLoginBranding (lib/identity.ts) controls styles and images only, not page behavior, so we can't add a message there. Options: (1) ask AWS for the feature (support case or re:Post); (2) build our own sign-up and confirm screens in the app with SignUp, ConfirmSignUp and ResendConfirmationCode, which changes ADR 0007 and needs a security review; revisit alongside 21q (landing page and sign-up). Raised by the owner while testing sign-up in prod, 2026-09-30.

title: Notice when two-step sign-in is turned off, and clean up notice rows on account deletion
description: From PR #278. (1) Turning TOTP off with SetUserMFAPreference sends nothing; add a twoStepOff notice through the same path. (2) A very late CloudTrail event during account deletion could leave a NOTICE# or NOTICE_ADDRESS row (possibly holding an address) in the deleted user's partition; add a TTL or have the function skip deleted users, and confirm the deletion purge covers these rows.
acceptance_criteria: Tests for both; security review.
notes: 2026-09-30 (PR #278 review): ConfirmForgotPassword and DeleteUser made directly also send no notice; consider them here.

title: Guard the security notices path: DLQ depth alarm, rule-tampering watch, alarm wording
description: From PR #278. (1) Alarm on the security-notices dead-letter queue's depth: an event EventBridge couldn't deliver doesn't reach SecurityNoticeFailures. (2) Cover the supply-checkout-<env>-security-notices rule with the rule-tampering watch, so disabling or deleting it alerts. (3) Update the 'Security notices failing' alarm text in infra/lib/observability/journey-alarms.ts to cover the CloudTrail path.
acceptance_criteria: DLQ alarm, tampering coverage and alarm text with infra tests.
notes: 2026-09-30: the DLQ depth alarm moved into PR #278 (review finding); this bead keeps the tampering watch and the alarm wording.

title: End a closed team's subscription at close, once reopen resumes it
description: From PR #275 (8jc.18). The early cancel (queued 'closed' message, worker sets cancel_at_period_end within seconds; commit 39fb70c in #275's history) was dropped because reopen doesn't resume subscriptions yet (85qp) and the worker can't record stripeCancelledFor, so a quick reopen would leave a paying team silently set to cancel. Bring it back after 85qp: record the cancel so reopen can resume it, either by letting the worker write stripeCancelledFor conditioned on purgeAfter (narrow IAM grant, security review) or with a Stripe metadata marker on the subscription. Also closes the small gap where the re-read after a Stripe change throws and a reopen goes unalarmed.
acceptance_criteria: A renewal within an hour of closing isn't charged; a reopen right after close resumes the subscription; tests; security review.

title: npm run operators: stop the remaining steps when Ctrl-C arrives between AWS CLI calls
description: From PR #274 (pbp.21). If Ctrl-C lands while scripts/operators.mjs itself is running (between AWS CLI calls) rather than while the CLI runs, Node never runs the script's SIGINT handler because the script's code is synchronous, so the remaining steps still run and it exits 0. Make an interrupt stop further steps and exit non-zero. Operator-pool tooling, so it needs a security review.
acceptance_criteria: A test that interrupts between two CLI calls sees no further calls and a non-zero exit; security review.

title: Tune the RUM event alarms and graph RUM ingestion on the dashboard
description: From PR #273 (3sv.7). Add a graph of RUM events ingested (AWS/RUM RumEventPayloadSize SampleCount) to the dashboard's web row, and after a few weeks of real traffic revisit the 100k/hour (P2) and 1M/hour (P1) thresholds. Optional second guard: a monthly AWS Budget on CloudWatch RUM cost, which needs SNS topic and KMS key policy grants for budgets.amazonaws.com (or email subscribers read from the alarm SSM parameters).
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard graph with an infra test; thresholds reviewed against real traffic and recorded; budget added or explicitly declined.

title: Lock the operator audit watch's log writes to its own function
description: From PR #259 (3sv.9). The operator audit watch role has the same unconditioned logs statement the group watch had, so another function given the role could write its logs and forge its heartbeat. Add the lambda:SourceFunctionArn condition (unqualified ARN from the fixed name) as #259 did for the group watch, update the test, and add the after-deploy check that the watch-silent alarm stays OK.
acceptance_criteria: The audit watch role's logs statement is conditioned on its own function; infra tests; security review.

title: Alarm when security notice emails fail
description: From PR #257 (8jc.15). SecurityNoticeFailures is only on the dashboard. Add a P2 alarm like 'Team closure emails failing', with a runbook entry.
acceptance_criteria: P2 alarm on SecurityNoticeFailures in the observability stack, with tests and a runbook link.

title: Route product price through money() in createProduct and updateProduct
description: From the PR #260 security review. backend/src/data/products.ts (around lines 34-37) checks price only as finite and >= 0 and stores it raw, with no upper limit or cents rule, the gap #260 closed in sheets.ts line(). Not reachable from handlers today (product routes use documents.ts and money()), so defence in depth. Also, if setSheetLine is ever wired to a handler, give line() the same allowance as documents.ts writtenMoney for an unchanged stored value.
acceptance_criteria: createProduct and updateProduct reject over-limit and sub-cent prices like the other money fields; backend tests.

title: Close the trail bucket's remaining exposure and object-deletion gaps
description: From the PR #256 security review. (1) The trail records no S3 data events, so DeleteObject/DeleteObjectVersion on log files can't alert; DeleteObjectVersion silently destroys a log file. Say so in the 'CloudTrail itself' residual-risk text in docs/infrastructure.md and point to Object Lock (owner decision in 3sv.4) as the fix. (2) Defence in depth: add PutBucketOwnershipControls, DeleteBucketOwnershipControls, PutBucketAcl, PutBucketPublicAccessBlock, DeleteBucketPublicAccessBlock (and consider PutBucketReplication) to the trail bucket rule's outside-deploy list (about 150 characters).
acceptance_criteria: Docs state the object-deletion gap; pattern tests cover the new events; size test passes.

title: Spike: advisory Claude check of journey step screenshots against the spec
description: Have Claude on Bedrock compare each step's end screenshot with that step's Expected text in docs/journeys.md and note mismatches in the evidence report. Advisory only, never gating. Measure cost per release and false-positive rate.
acceptance_criteria:
- Report section with per-step verdicts and reasons
- Cost per release and false-positive rate written up

title: Bring docs/journeys.md's Status column up to date
description: Found while recording the journey videos (PR #245). The Status column and text are stale: J0 is listed as Planned though sign-in is built (zsm, l5y closed); J9's server-side roles are called planned though dj6 is closed; J2 still calls the import planned though ig9 is closed. Check every journey's status against closed beads and the tests.
notes: Folded into supply-checkout-s3c.3 (the registry computes the Status column).

title: Condition the entitlement check's fix on the team's version, not field values
description: From the PR #229 security review (Low, finding 1). applySubscription(..., asRead) compares status, plan, seats and subscription ID, so an A->B->A sequence of events between the nightly check's read and write lets it write stale state, and cancelAtPeriodEnd/currentPeriodEnd aren't compared at all. Read the team's version (or stripeSyncedAt) in getBillingTeam and condition the write on it. Needs the attribute in BILLING_READ_ATTRIBUTES: an IAM change, so it needs a security review.

title: Seat queue: stop a sender suppressing another customer's nightly sync via dedupe IDs
description: From the PR #233 security review (Low). The seat sync FIFO queue uses queue-wide dedupe, and the nightly reconcile's dedupe ID is predictable (reconcile-<day>-<customer>). Any sender (the account and ops functions) could send that ID just before the run with another customer's body, and the real reconcile for that customer would be dropped for the night. No Stripe change is possible. Fix: have the worker refuse a seat sync whose body customer differs from the record's MessageGroupId, and/or set deduplicationScope MESSAGE_GROUP with fifoThroughputLimit PER_MESSAGE_GROUP_ID.

title: Let owners of a closed team see and download invoices before deletion
description: From PR #231 (eja). The invoices route refuses a closed team and the team bar hides the button, so during the 30 days before purge an owner can't get their invoices in the app. Allow listing for closed-but-not-purged teams, owner-only with the same MFA rules.

title: Nightly entitlement check: flag a second live subscription for a customer
description: From PR #229 (8jc.9). When a team's own subscription is live, the check doesn't list the customer's other subscriptions, so a stray duplicate whose events were lost isn't caught. List them and count and alert on extras (see 8jc.11 for refunding a paid duplicate).

title: Email owners when the nightly entitlement check fixes drift
description: From PR #229 (8jc.9). When the nightly check corrects a team's status or plan, no billing email is sent (only replaying the lost event would send one). Have the worker send the matching notice (e.g. read-only) itself, using the SQS message ID as the claim key so it sends once.

title: Make main's required CI check strict, or correct CLAUDE.md
description: From PR #227: the 'Protect main' ruleset has strict_required_status_checks_policy false, but CLAUDE.md says branches must be up to date. npm run land updates branches in practice. Owner: turn on 'require branches to be up to date' in the ruleset, or the lead corrects CLAUDE.md. Also noted: CI doesn't check Signed-off-by, and the ruleset requires 0 approving reviews (the agent security review stands in).
notes: 2026-10-01: this bit us. #305 (infra test App with cdk.json flags) merged green without re-running on top of #301 (new IAM statements), so main's infra snapshots broke; later main runs were cancelled or skipped the infra job by path filter, so main looked green. Fixed in #313. Turning on 'require branches to be up to date' (or a merge queue) prevents this.

title: Decide: build the keep-receipt-photos team setting, or drop it from ADR 0008 and the terms
description: From the privacy policy draft (PR #223): ADR 0008 and terms section 9 promise a team setting to keep receipt photos encrypted for 90 days. Nothing builds it and no bead covers it. Decide, then either add a build bead or remove it from ADR 0008, the terms and the privacy policy.

title: Self-host the web app's fonts instead of loading them from Google
description: From the privacy policy draft (PR #223): the app loads fonts from Google Fonts, which sends every visitor's IP address to Google. Bundle the fonts with the build, drop fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com from the CSP, and remove Google Fonts from the privacy policy's subprocessors.

title: Seat sync hardening from the PR #213 review
description: From PR #213 (l50) and its security review. (1) Queue a seat sync from restore's removeMember (data/restore.ts) and operator reopen; today the nightly run fixes them and counts drift. (2) Cap the billing worker's event source maximumConcurrency on the seat queue so the nightly fan-out stays under Stripe's rate limit. (3) The reconcile message id is fixed per day and goes into the Stripe idempotency key, so a same-day rerun can replay a cached no-op and log 'updated'; use a per-run id or fold the SQS messageId into the key. (4) Don't update when billed members exceed MEMBERS_PER_TEAM; log, count and let the drift alarm surface it. (5) Compare team.stripeCustomerId with the message's customer and return not_ours early; log a warning on not_ours. (6) parseMessage should return only picked fields or reject 'kind'. (7) Note in docs/infrastructure.md that the primary-region reconciler also covers us-west-2 teams and converges because quantity is recomputed.
acceptance_criteria: Each point done or explicitly dropped with a reason; tests for 1, 3, 4, 5, 6.

title: Turn on Sign in with Apple in prod
description: Split from fdi by the ADR 0007 review (2026-09-28). Create the Sign in with Apple service ID and key once the paid Apple Developer account exists (needs the business entity and D-U-N-S number, ar0), store them, and turn Apple on in the prod pool. Required before the iOS app offers Google sign-in.

title: Alarm on closed-team subscriptions not found in Stripe, and stop permanent failures starving the purge's cancel list
description: From the PR #210 security review. (1) team-purge-handler records resource_missing as done with only a warning; a Stripe mode or key mismatch would mark every closed team done with none cancelled. Add a metric and an alarm on count > 0. (2) listClosedTeamsToEnd takes the first 100 eligible teams and failures stay eligible, so 100 permanent failures (e.g. CustomerMismatch) block newer closures. Record permanent failures separately or skip them, and log when listed equals the limit.
acceptance_criteria: Metric and alarm exist with a test; a test shows permanent failures don't block newer teams.

title: Customer Portal hardening from the PR #194 review
description: (1) src/aws/account.js manageBilling and subscribe: parse the returned URL and require https with host billing.stripe.com / checkout.stripe.com before navigating, else show the error. (2) backend/src/billing/portal.ts: pin login_page.enabled=false and compare it so stripe-catalog drives it back. (3) docs/infrastructure.md: note a removed owner can use an already-issued portal session until Stripe expires it. (4) Don't count Stripe rate_limit errors toward the Billing portal broken P1 alarm (or add a per-caller limit); same for checkout. (5) account-handler teamBody: store and return cancel_at exactly when set without cancel_at_period_end. (6) portalConfigurationResolver: page past the first 100 configurations.
acceptance_criteria: Each item fixed with tests or documented; security review for (1) and (2).

title: RUM scrub follow-ups from the PR #195 re-review
description: (1) src/aws/rum.js URL_QUERY is quadratic on long runs of '/' without spaces/?/#; truncate each string (e.g. 4 KB) before scrubbing. acceptance_criteria: Timing cause found and fixed; passes a 25x repeat in CI.

title: Remove a sheet line without recreating a deleted sheet in the artifact build
description: After PR #82, the artifact build still reads then writes the sheet to remove a line; if the sheet is deleted between the two, the write can recreate it (claude.ai's db has no conditional write).
acceptance_criteria: Removing a line can't recreate a deleted sheet even in that window (e.g. a field-delete update if the runtime supports one); test in the artifact build.

title: Copy backups to us-west-2
description: Add a second copy action from the backup account's vault to us-west-2 (PR #80).
acceptance_criteria: The copy lands in us-west-2 with a compliance lock; tests assert it.

title: Show members' names on the members screen
description: MEMBER items store only an email, so the members screen shows emails (PR #78).
acceptance_criteria: A display name from Cognito is stored when someone creates a team or accepts an invite, returned from GET /members and shown; names never logged; security review for the PII handling.

title: Let contributors and viewers leave a team from the web app
description: The members API lets anyone leave, but only owners get a UI (PR #78).
acceptance_criteria: Non-owners see a Leave team action with two-tap confirm; it calls DELETE /teams/{teamId}/members/{me} then shows the access-changed screen; Playwright test.

title: Let someone stop counting an item in the web build
description: Clearing 'In storage now' on a counted item leaves stock unchanged in the web build because the stock command can't uncount (PR #76); in the artifact it removes the count.
acceptance_criteria: Clearing the field stops counting and records a movement (e.g. a reason 'uncount' stock command); the drift check handles it; tests in the web build.

title: Alarm when SES sending nears the daily quota
description: Listed in docs/journeys.md but not built (PR #73).
acceptance_criteria: A P2 alarm fires when sends exceed 80% of the SES daily quota; test in infra/test/observability.test.ts.

title: Live-update consumer follow-ups from the PR #71 review
description: (a) schema.ts and docs say the consumer can't read emails; it can via stream images, so say 'through the table'; ensure nothing logs raw stream events. (b) call audience.recipients(teamId) per chunk so the cut-off bound doesn't depend on the Lambda timeout.
acceptance_criteria: Docs corrected; a test asserts raw events aren't logged; recipients re-read per chunk with a test.
notes: PR #114 review: (c) clients should skip an eventId they've already seen, since a stuck batch now resends up to 25 times; (d) give the consumer's DynamoDB client a request timeout (~2 s) so the recipient read can't push an invocation past 10 s.

title: Tighten the import's transaction-size error match and test table measure
description: PR #67 review follow-ups: transactionTooLarge in backend/src/data/imports.ts matches /size|large|4 ?MB/i and drops the original error on the 413 path; backend/test/memory-table.ts measures transactions with plain JSON.stringify, undercounting constructor-keyed Maps.
acceptance_criteria: The match is exactly the two known DynamoDB messages; reaching k=1 logs error.name and a truncated message (never item data); the test table uses the Map-expanding replacer for transaction and item size checks; tests cover a non-size ValidationException surfacing as 500.

title: Drop a team from the switcher when the user is removed from it
description: With per-member channels (PR #71), nothing tells the web app when another of the user's teams removes them until its next fetch.
acceptance_criteria: When a user is removed from a team they aren't viewing, the team switcher drops it on the next /me refresh or re-list; tested with the fake backend.

title: Let a signed-in user link Google or Apple from account settings
description: Automatic linking (0b1) can't cover an Apple user hiding their email (relay address) or a provider email different from the account's.
acceptance_criteria: A signed-in native user can start a provider link from settings that links that identity to their own sub only; tests cover a relay address and refusing an identity already on another user.

title: Restore branch-coverage headroom in the artifact build
description: After PR #69 the artifact build's branch coverage is 98.05% (17 uncovered) because it can never take web-only branches such as the command path in src/moves.js. Exclude or restructure build-specific code so each build's gate measures reachable branches, or add tests.
acceptance_criteria: Artifact branch coverage has at least 0.5 points of headroom over the 98% gate without lowering it; approach documented in docs/testing.md.

title: Treat lookalike item names as the same item
description: Name matching (import nameKey and the app) doesn't strip zero-width or bidi characters, so near-identical names create lookalike duplicates (PR #67 review).
acceptance_criteria: Names differing only by \p{Cf} characters match the same item; bidi override characters are rejected in names; tests in import and the app.

title: Limit inventory imports per team instead of per route
description: The import route's API Gateway throttle (5/s, burst 10) is shared across all callers, so one team's imports can get every other team 429s (PR #67 review). Add a per-team limit, e.g. a DynamoDB counter like the team-creation limit.
acceptance_criteria: One team hitting its import limit doesn't affect another team's imports; tests cover it.

title: Retry a failed background token refresh
description: In src/aws/session.js background(), a scheduled refresh that fails as unavailable (including a timeout) doesn't re-arm a timer, so the live socket's token can go stale until the next API 401 (PR #61 review). Also use a try per key in signOut's storage cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: A background refresh that fails as unavailable retries after about 60 s; tests cover a failure then a successful retry; signOut cleanup clears remaining keys when one removeItem throws.

title: Alarm when the email_verified trigger fails
description: The 6v9 pre token generation trigger doesn't throw on a failed AdminUpdateUserAttributes, so the Lambda Errors alarm won't catch it and users silently stay unverified (PR #65).
acceptance_criteria: A metric or metric filter on the trigger's failure log feeds an alarm and the dashboard; test in infra/test/observability.test.ts; entry in docs/journeys.md (J3).
notes: Cover both the 'failed' and 'downgrade-failed' outcomes from PR #65.

title: Queue each document's writes in the web adapter
description: Two quick writes to the same document from one page can 409 against the page's own earlier write, because the second is sent before the first response updates the held version (PR #64 review). Serialize writes per document in src/aws/db.js.
acceptance_criteria: Two rapid edits to one document from the same page both save without a conflict message; a real conflict from another user still shows it; tests cover both.

title: Alarm when the Cognito revoke fails on sign-out
description: backend/src/api/auth-handler.ts clears the cookie and returns 204 even when the Cognito revoke fails, logging only a warning; the refresh token stays valid at Cognito until expiry. Add a metric and alarm on that warning (found in PR #61 review).
acceptance_criteria: A metric filter or EMF metric counts revoke failures; an alarm fires on repeated failures; test or snapshot covers it.

title: Retry non-conflicting checkouts automatically instead of showing a conflict
description: With required versions (3q9), two people adding different items to the same sheet at once get a 409 though their changes don't clash. Mostly solved by the server commands; handle what remains.
acceptance_criteria: When a checkout or return hits a 409, the page applies its quantity to the latest line and retries once; the conflict message shows only for edit screens or when the retry also fails; tests cover both.

title: Record each web release's channel explicitly
description: publish-web activate infers a release's channel from whether it has a config.json. Write a release.json marker ({channel, commit, builtAt}) at publish time and use it.
acceptance_criteria: publish uploads releases/<v>/release.json; activate checks it, falling back to the config.json check for older releases; status shows each release's channel; tests in scripts/publish-web.test.mjs.

title: Key the receipt draft by team
description: The receipt draft is one shared localStorage key. Sign-out clears it (83z), but switching teams still shows one team's draft in another. Store it per team in the web build.
acceptance_criteria: The draft is stored per team (e.g. supplyCheckout.receiptDraft.<teamId>) in the web build and unchanged in the artifact; switching teams shows only that team's draft; sign-out clears every team's draft; tests cover both.

title: Harden the edge router and the publish script (review follow-ups from PR #60)
description: All Low/Info from the PR #60 review. L1: router.js 503 response lacks HSTS and nosniff; share a SECURITY_HEADERS object with redirect(). L2: web-stack.ts routerCode() uses String.replace with string replacements ($& patterns); use a replacer function or validate hosts against ^[a-z0-9.-]+$. L3: publish-web.mjs activate doesn't check the release's channel, so activating an app release on the demo channel would serve the app build and its config.json at /demo/; require the version to match the channel. L4: add router tests for trailing-dot and port hosts and an encoded-traversal (/demo/..%2f..%2freleases/x) rewrite case.
acceptance_criteria: All four addressed with tests.

title: Inventory search ignores barcodes typed in a different case
description: pickOutModal lowercases the search text but compares it to the barcode as stored (String(p.code).includes(q)), so typing 'sku' or 'SKU' never matches a code like 'SKU1'. Numeric barcodes are unaffected. Found while adding coverage tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- Searching 'sku1' or 'SKU1' finds an item with code SKU1
- Test added in tests/sheets.spec.js

title: Add a PWA manifest, icons and offline shell
description: Install to home screen with the right icon and name; offline page when there's no signal.
acceptance_criteria: - Lighthouse installable check passes

title: Publish a public status page
description: Status page fed by the synthetic canaries.
acceptance_criteria: - status.<domain> live

title: Publish a subprocessor list and data processing addendum
description: Business customers will ask for these once teams get bigger.
acceptance_criteria:
- /subprocessors page
- DPA template customers can sign

title: Harden npm run land and beads:pr: atomic export checks, clearer errors, time limits
description: From the PR #270/#272 re-review. (1) beads-pr checks an export PR's files, then the nested land reads its head separately: pass the checked SHA to land (or read files and headRefOid together) so a push in between can't be merged. (2) A rename onto .beads/issues.jsonl passes the files check; also require changedFiles == 1. (3) Add </dev/null to the nested npm run land inside the while-read loop. (4) In land's merge-retry loop, a failed 'gh pr view headRefOid' reports 'changed after CI passed'; report the GitHub error instead. (5) 'gh pr checks --watch' has no time limit; bound it. (6) A head read racing gh pr update-branch can give a false 'changed' failure.
acceptance_criteria: Each item fixed or explicitly declined, with test cases in land-pr.test.sh / beads-pr.test.sh.

title: beads:pr: close duplicate open export PRs, not just land the oldest
description: From PR #272 (pbp.16). beads-pr.sh now lands the oldest open chore/beads-export-* PR instead of opening another, but any other open duplicates stay open and must be closed by hand. After landing the oldest, close the rest with a comment (their content is superseded by the fresh export).
acceptance_criteria: beads-pr.test.sh case: two open export PRs, the oldest lands and the other is closed.

title: Find out whether failed CloudTrail calls reach EventBridge, to make alert drills non-destructive
description: From PR #256/#259. If calls that fail with an errorCode (for example AccessDenied) still reach EventBridge and match the operator and trail rules, drills could use deliberately failing calls instead of real changes. Confirm on the real account and update the drill rows in docs/infrastructure.md.
acceptance_criteria: Documented answer; drill rows updated if failed calls alert.

title: Page through older invoices in the app
description: From PR #231 (eja). The list shows the latest 24 invoices and points to the Customer Portal for older ones. Add paging with starting_after, validating the in_ ID on the server.

title: Clean up null lines in stored artifact sheets
description: From PR #139: removed sheet lines in the artifact build stay as null entries in the stored document. Clean them up safely (e.g. on the next whole-sheet save) or document that they're harmless (export, totals, import from #129).
acceptance_criteria: Either nulls are dropped on a safe write with a test, or docs state why they're harmless and the export/import ignore them (test).

title: Sort the operator team list newest first
description: PR #142: paged ops team list follows team ID order since GSI3 sorts by ID.
acceptance_criteria: Team META items get a creation-time sort key in a separate index or partition, backfilled; one-team lookup still works; list pages newest first with bounded reads.

title: Guard invites made before invite guards existed
description: PR #140: live invites created before INVITEGUARD items have none, so a create racing a resend of one could still leave two live invites until they're re-sent or expire (≤30 days).
acceptance_criteria: A backfill writes guard items for existing live invites, or it's recorded as accepted risk once 30 days pass after deploy; test.

title: Promote a remaining member to owner in the restore tool
description: PR #123 leaves a deleted account that was the last owner of an open team with other members for a person to decide, via a hand-written transaction.
acceptance_criteria: A script mode promotes a named member to owner, moving counts and writing an audit entry; tests.

title: Refresh the account screen's email after the verify dialog finds a changed address
description: PR #111: after email_changed the dialog shows the new address but the prompt behind it keeps the old one until verified.
acceptance_criteria: After email_changed, the account screen prompt and team bar show the address from the reloaded /me; Playwright test.

title: Say only a bug can cause stock drift
description: After PR #84 document writes can't set stock, so docs/journeys.md J4, the drift-check bead and the alarm runbook shouldn't name 'a document write that set stock' as a cause.
acceptance_criteria: J4, the drift-check bead text and the alarm runbook say only a bug can cause drift.
notes: PR #124 added a 'delete' movement reason (delta -stock, count 0) on product delete; the drift check and any stock-history view must handle it.

title: Remove the last unreachable fallbacks in src/main.js
description: The || {} fallbacks around pickReturnModal/lineModal/returnModal/remove (main.js ~295, 342, 354, 368) can't be reached when the line exists (PR #79).
acceptance_criteria: Removed or covered by tests; artifact branch coverage at or above 99%.

title: Merge Google/Apple accounts created before automatic linking
description: Federated users created before the 0b1 trigger that share a verified email with a native user stay separate. Providers are off in prod so this may be empty; run before or right after enabling (fdi).
acceptance_criteria: A one-off script or runbook finds pairs by verified email and merges or reports them; never touches unverified emails.

title: Return permission_denied for viewers on every write route
description: The viewer's 403 on some routes carries invalid_argument, not permission_denied (PR #67 review; predates it).
acceptance_criteria: Every write route returns 403 permission_denied for viewers; tests assert the code.

title: Stream very large team exports
description: The client-side export builds one string in memory; only needed if teams get very large.
acceptance_criteria: When a team's documents exceed about 50 MB, the export is built in pieces rather than one in-memory string.

title: Sync the theme across open tabs
description: Listen for the storage event so a theme change in one tab applies to the device's other open tabs.
acceptance_criteria: Changing the theme in one tab updates data-theme and the pressed button in another open tab without reload; tested in both builds; coverage stays at 98%.
notes:
Implemented in PR #152. Local validation: all 9 theme tests pass in desktop Chrome in both artifact and web builds; ESLint passes. CI and coverage checks pending.
PR #152 CI passed, including artifact/web desktop Chrome coverage at the required 98% and both iPhone Safari jobs. Ready for review and merge.

title: CSV filename has a stray space when a sheet has no date
description: exportCsv builds `${client} ${date}.csv` and trims the whole string, so a sheet without a date downloads as 'Client .csv'. Only sheets saved without a date (old data) hit this; the form requires a date. Found by tests/legacy-data.spec.js.
acceptance_criteria:
- A dateless sheet downloads as 'Client.csv'
- legacy-data test asserts the exact filename
